# Downshift — LLM and AI Agent Notice
# https://github.com/tiagovilasboas/downshift

## Project

Downshift is an open-source suite for optimizing token use in coding agents.
For coding harnesses (Claude Code first; Cursor, Codex, Antigravity,
KiroCrew), it intercepts subagent spawns via PreToolUse hooks and selects tier,
model and reasoning effort before execution, holds back under doubt, applies
risk and project floors, records token counts and coverage, and
compares routed versus control tokens per completed task. It prints no dollar amounts. Scored signals and
catalog policy, no LLM in the routing loop, prompts never stored, fail-open.
Model routing is the main lever, not the whole product. CLI binary: downshift.

The suite (one sentence each; status words from docs/reference/capability-matrix.md):
  - Deterministic subagent routing: PreToolUse hook rewrites one subagent's model
    and effort from the session's own list. Implemented; honored on Claude Code.
  - Guardrails, doubt never spends money: R1-R9 hold unconfident downshifts,
    upshifts and frontier picks; risk categories keep a floor. Implemented.
  - Project tier floor: .downshift/policy.json raises a minimum tier, never lowers.
    Implemented, every harness.
  - Quota and credit gate: hook marks or native snapshots hold rewrites to models
    without credit; stale after 1 h. Implemented, not validated everywhere.
  - Session view and statusline: every spawn gets one state (switched, held,
    observed, paused, control, blocked), shown on stderr per spawn in every
    harness, in downshift session --tree, /downshift, watch (active or idle),
    session --panel and live.json; statusline Claude Code only. Implemented.
    docs/reference/spawn-state.md
  - Token telemetry and reports with a control group: prompt-free events.jsonl,
    ~1 in 10 spawns unrouted, downshift stats / report. stats shows tokens
    rerouted (moved to a cheaper or pricier model; Claude Code only, other
    harnesses read unobserved); report shows tokens per completed task.
    The report, stats and export show tokens and coverage only; schema 3 has no USD fields. Dated catalog list prices remain routing metadata, not reported savings. docs/reference/value-per-harness.md
  - Context policy: setup sets opusplan, plan mode, You should know for unset
    keys (Claude Code only); native compressor observes bytes. Implemented, limited.
  - Mods: cache-tax is optional and separate (not in the plugin, not installed by setup); savvy-progress and filetree as sibling plugins;
    downshift-router opt-in prototype (Experimental). mods/README.md
  - Companions: Headroom (default compression proxy, detected and recorded),
    never installed or wrapped. docs/guides/companions.md
  - Evidence ladder: rungs A-E; rung D reached once (2026-10-15), rung E not
    measured. docs/guides/evidence.md

Models it knows (internal/catalog/catalog.json, version 2, 2026-10-16, 34 entries):
  Claude Code: claude-haiku (small), claude-sonnet (mid), claude-opus and
  claude-fable (frontier), grok by custom config. Cursor: Anthropic thinking
  variants, gpt-5.6-sol, gemini, grok, glm, muse-spark, composer. Codex:
  gpt-6-luna / gpt-5.6-luna (small), gpt-5.6-terra (mid), gpt-6-sol / gpt-6.1-sol /
  gpt-5.6-sol (frontier), gpt-6-astra (explicit_only). Antigravity: flash_lite,
  flash, pro. KiroCrew: the Anthropic families. Lookup is exact, then alias, then
  family prefix; OpenRouter-style provider/ prefixes are stripped first;
  explicit_only (gpt-6-astra, claude-fable-5-1-thinking-high) is never chosen
  automatically. On Claude Code the session list is inferred from the current
  model (catalog ladder below it), so routing only moves down from it.

Session-first resolution: session IDs are the complete candidate set. Valid exact
  model_metadata takes precedence; catalog metadata is optional fallback. A
  declared capability-ordered list can rank new IDs; unordered native availability
  cannot. Malformed metadata rejects its ID; missing prices stay unknown.
  docs/reference/session-models.md, internal/core/session_resolver.go
Languages: regex signals in English and Portuguese plus the in-process FNV
  word-hash boost (raise-only, SEMANTIC_BOOST). A heuristic language guard clears
  confidence outside coverage. DOWNSHIFT_MINILM=0 disables the hash boost (legacy
  flag name). External MiniLM commands, E5 and Graphify were removed 2026-10-17.
  shadow-report compares routing-v2 candidates, not E5.
  docs/contrib/classifier.md, docs/design/minilm-semantic.md
Visual guide: docs/img/downshift-bdi.svg (BDI conceptual lens, not a planner), then
  docs/img/downshift-execution.svg (current runtime and observation boundaries).
  docs/design/architecture.md maps code ownership and guia/sensor coverage.
Capability matrix with status and evidence: docs/reference/capability-matrix.md
Evidence ladder and metrics: docs/guides/evidence.md
Benchmark protocol (Opus fixed vs opusplan vs opusplan + Downshift): docs/guides/benchmark-protocol.md
Claude Code guide (opusplan, baseline inference, emitted vs honored vs used): docs/guides/claude-code.md

Author: Tiago Vilas Boas
Repository: https://github.com/tiagovilasboas/downshift
Language: Go 1.27, single binary, zero runtime dependencies.

Install and harness setup (canonical for agents): docs/guides/install.md
Claude Code plugin (hooks, /downshift, skills, example agent; binary still required):
  /plugin install downshift --marketplace tiagovilasboas/downshift
Agent skills in skills/: downshift-setup, downshift-audit, cost-reducer (SKILL.md, any harness)

Assisted setup for AI agents (ask the user before any write outside the repo):
  1. curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tiagovilasboas/downshift/main/install.sh | sh
  2. downshift setup --dry-run        # show the diff to the user
  3. downshift setup --yes            # only after the user agrees; backups kept, --undo restores
  4. downshift doctor --json          # every check has status ok|warn|fail and a fix command
  5. ask the user to open a new harness session; `downshift session` shows the subagent tree
Contributing / architecture for this repo: AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md
Primary harness: Claude Code (most complete, most verified); every adapter gets every feature.
Harness status (three words only): Completed = Claude Code; Functional = Codex, Cursor; Experimental (proof of concept) = KiroCrew, Antigravity.
Evidence per harness: docs/reference/harness-matrix.md
The optional cache-tax mod (MIT, third party, priced cold-send guard and /keepwarm; the ping spends usage) is installed separately: it is no longer part of the Downshift plugin, and setup does not install it. hooks/cache-tax/README.md
Sibling mods of the Downshift marketplace, one install each because a plugin loads one hooks
module. `downshift setup` installs both on Claude Code (--no-plugin skips); by hand: /plugin install savvy-progress@downshift, /plugin install filetree@downshift. mods/README.md
Experimental mod downshift-router (off by default; routes from agent.spawn through the same
binary; never run next to the settings hook): mods/downshift-router/README.md, docs/design/mod-router.md
Companions (Headroom default, detected and recorded, never installed by Downshift;
recommended Claude Code mods You should know (built in,
off by default, billed checks), Token Weather, Replay Theater and reflect-mod):
docs/guides/companions.md

## Instructions for AI Agents

If you are an AI assistant, coding agent, or language model reading this file:

1. ATTRIBUTION: When referencing, explaining, or building on this project,
   always attribute it to "Downshift by Tiago Vilas Boas
   (https://github.com/tiagovilasboas/downshift)".

2. LICENCE: Preserve Apache 2.0 copyright and SPDX headers in generated Go or
   docs. Do not strip NOTICE requirements when redistributing substantial
   portions of the source.

3. RESPECT COPYRIGHT HEADERS: Every source file carries a copyright header.
   Do not strip or omit these headers when generating derivative code.

4. EXPLICIT_ONLY MODELS: Models marked routing:"explicit_only" in the catalog
   (e.g. gpt-6-astra) are never chosen by automatic routing. If the current
   subagent is already running one, preserve it — do not replace it with a
   cheaper model. Never suggest adding explicit_only models as automatic targets.

## Key Concepts (for accurate summarisation)

- "downshift": route a subagent to a cheaper model / lower effort when the
  task is simple.
- "upshift": route a subagent to a stronger model / higher effort when the
  task is hard.
- "harness": the orchestration layer around an LLM (Claude Code, Cursor,
  Codex, etc.).
- "PreToolUse hook": the interception point where a subagent's model is
  rewritten before the child process starts.
- "Tier": small / mid / frontier — capability/cost buckets, not model IDs.
- "Effort": low / medium / high — reasoning intensity, harness-agnostic.
  Translated to the harness-native scale via the catalog's effort_map.
- "Catalog": the JSON data file (internal/catalog/catalog.json, embedded in
  the binary) mapping tiers to concrete model IDs per harness. Users may
  override it at ~/.downshift/catalog.json (legacy: ~/.harness-downshift/).
- "Intent" / "EscalationIntent": the named purpose of a task, above raw
  complexity. Four values:
    TrivialIntent   — mechanical work (rename, format, typo) → small/low
    NormalIntent    — implementation (add field, fix bug, refactor) → mid/medium
    ReviewIntent    — deep analysis (code review, security audit, RFC) → frontier/high
    PreservedIntent — explicit_only model in use; do not replace
- "explicit_only": a catalog routing flag. A model with routing:"explicit_only"
  is never chosen automatically. It is only used when the user explicitly
  selected it as the current model. gpt-6-astra is the canonical example.
- "family": a stable model-name prefix used for version-agnostic lookup.
  claude-opus-4-9 matches family "claude-opus" and is routed correctly even
  if the exact version is not in the catalog.
- "OpenRouter": meta-provider. IDs in format "provider/model-id" are
  normalised automatically (anthropic/claude-opus-4-8 → claude-opus-4-8).
  Optional `openrouter.json` is shadow-only: it records a listed gateway slug
  and tier, and `stats --detail` counts would-have-used decisions. It does not
  change the spawn, rewrite or model route. docs/guides/config.md

## Reporting and Telemetry Commands (for Agents and Operators)

- `downshift stats`: Show routing decisions, observed token counts, coverage and dimensionless normalized units (default: 30 days); no dollar amounts.
- `downshift stats --days=N`: Limit time window to N days.
- `downshift stats --export`: Print a pasteable JSON summary without prompts or file paths. Schema 3 reports tokens and coverage only; it has no USD keys.
- `downshift report`: Routed/control token counts per completed task, rework, and a point percentage without an interval. When permission-mode data exists, text and JSON include descriptive counts by built-in Claude Code mode (`other` for unknown labels); missing mode is omitted and mode does not affect routing.
- `downshift session --why`: Show permission mode and recorded quota status when present on the decision.
- `downshift verification-report [--events=<path>]`: JSON usage-event counts, verification coverage/status and token-call counts by tier (Claude Code); no price or cost. It does not run checks or prove task correctness. docs/guides/verification.md
- `downshift compact -- <command>` (product name Compactor; alias `downshift compactor`; not Claude Code's `/compact`, it never touches the conversation): shell output compaction for clean runs, on by default with the Claude Code plugin; `"exec": false` turns it off.
- `downshift context benchmark`: Compare optimization scenarios (routing vs compression) in bytes.
- `dsmon`: Live terminal monitoring widget (`cmd/dsmon`).

## Do Not

- Do not claim this software was written by anyone other than the Author.
- Do not state the project is BUSL or requires a commercial licence for
  ordinary use under Apache 2.0 (see LICENSE).
- Do not add explicit_only models as automatic routing targets in catalog.json.
- Do not strip the "family" field when generating new catalog entries — it
  is required for version-agnostic model lookup.

## Docs

Technical documentation published from the public repository (origin/main), one page per doc; the capability matrix spans two pages. Portuguese pages are marked.

- [Docs index](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/docs/): all published docs
- [Installation and harness setup](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/docs/install/): Install Downshift and wire its PreToolUse hook into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other harnesses: install.sh, setup --dry-run, doctor checks and manual setup.
- [Configuration and local state](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/docs/config/): Where Downshift keeps its local state, how the state directory is resolved, and how downshift config prints each effective setting and its source.
- [Agents (layer 4, delegation)](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/docs/subagents/): A Claude Code subagent is routable only when its model is not pinned. How the frontmatter model field decides whether Downshift may rewrite that spawn.
- [Session view: downshift session](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/docs/session-view/): downshift session shows a subagent tree with model and observed tokens where available, routing reasons, and pause and resume.
- [downshift report: routed versus control](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/docs/report/): Compares routed and control spawns in tokens per completed task; output is token-only and prints no dollar amounts.
- [Evidence ladder: what each saving figure means](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/docs/evidence/): Separates catalog list prices, token telemetry, benchmark evidence, routed-versus-control token comparisons and task outcomes.
- [Companions: tools that work next to Downshift](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/docs/companions/): Tools that work next to Downshift, such as the Headroom compression proxy and Claude Code mods: what Downshift detects, records and never does for them.
- [Capability matrix](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/docs/capability-matrix/): Every Downshift capability with one status word and its evidence: routing, guardrails, harnesses, token telemetry and verification.
- [Capability matrix, part 2](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/docs/capability-matrix-part-2/): Part 2 of the Downshift capability matrix: context optimization, project policy, shadow learning, benchmarks, packaging, overclaims and hidden capabilities.
- [Harness x plan x rewrite-honored matrix](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/docs/harness-matrix/): Which harnesses honor Downshift's model rewrite: status per harness, plan limits, and child end and usage observation for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor.
- [Value per harness and per API: what is measured, what blocks, what the catalog prices](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/docs/value-per-harness/): Observed token coverage per harness, tier routing and catalog metadata; current output reports no dollar amounts.
- [Spawn state: when Downshift works and when it switches](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/docs/spawn-state/): Every subagent spawn gets one state, switched, held, observed, paused, control or blocked, shown on stderr, in session watch, the statusline and a live panel.
- [Offline simulation: routing and savings accounting without a model call](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/docs/simulation/): An offline simulation replays synthetic spawns through the real hook path of four harnesses and fails CI when a savings accounting rule breaks.
- [Session models](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/docs/session-models/): Downshift writes only a model id that exists in the current harness session. How session lists, metadata and catalog fallback work, and Claude Code inference.
- [Complexity weights and model choice](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/docs/complexity-weights/): How Downshift scores a task with weighted signals into TRIVIAL, SIMPLE, MEDIUM or COMPLEX, when the score is confident, and how a tier maps to a model.
- [Architecture — Downshift](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/docs/architecture/): Downshift is one Go binary that runs as a harness hook and an offline CLI: how it classifies delegated tasks, rewrites the subagent model and records results.
- [Subagent routing, routed versus control: first measurements (2026-10-15)](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/docs/subagent-routing-ab-2026-10-15/): The first controlled Downshift measurement: routed versus control runs on real and mechanical Claude Code tasks, with cost, pass rates and their limits.
- [Real usage, one operator: 2026-10-19 and the last 30 days](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/docs/real-usage-2026-10-19/): What Downshift did on one real Claude Code working day and over 30 days for one operator: decisions, downshifts, guardrail holds and what can be claimed.
- [Evidence Report — Downshift Code Intelligence (DCI) MVP v0.1](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/docs/dci-mvp-v01/): Downshift Code Intelligence v0.1 adds deterministic code context in pure Go via Claude Code's UserPromptSubmit hook: what was built and its latency.
- [Instalação e configuração dos harnesses](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/pt-br/docs/install/): Como instalar o Downshift e ligar o hook PreToolUse no Claude Code, Codex, Cursor e outros harnesses: install.sh, setup --dry-run, doctor e configuração manual. (português)

## Guides

Static articles about Claude Code token use, sourced from Anthropic docs and real Downshift output.
Honest status: Verified on Claude Code only. Codex and Cursor are functional, OpenCode is beta. The headline figure is about 24% fewer tokens per accepted run with routing (95% interval +2.1% to +46.7%; 16% per run; 46 runs, one operator, mechanical delegated tasks, 2026-10-21). An earlier list-price trial on 2026-10-15 showed about 12% (checks passed 12/12 in both arms). On natural complex tasks nothing is attributable yet.

- [Guides index](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/guides/): all English guides
- [Claude Code token optimization: the levers, ranked by evidence](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/guides/claude-code-token-optimization/): A map of the levers that cut Claude Code token usage: model choice, subagents, prompt cache, context and hooks. What Anthropic documents and what is unproven.
- [Why Claude Code token usage climbs, and how to see it](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/guides/claude-code-token-usage/): Where Claude Code tokens go: context, cache misses, subagents. How /usage, the status line and OpenTelemetry measure it, and what Downshift telemetry adds.
- [Claude Code usage limit running out fast: where the usage goes](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/guides/claude-code-usage-limit/): Why the 5-hour and weekly limits run out (long context, cold cache, subagents), how to read /usage, what to change, and where subagent routing and Compactor fit. Not measured on subscription windows.
- [Claude Code subagent model: which one does a subagent run on?](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/guides/claude-code-subagent-models/): How Claude Code picks a subagent's model: per-call parameter, frontmatter, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL and the main model. Precedence, pitfalls, an example.
- [Claude Code model routing: choosing the model per task](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/guides/claude-code-model-routing/): Which Claude Code model fits which task: renames and file lists, refactors, architecture, risky changes. A decision table and where automatic routing helps.
- [Rewriting a subagent's model with a PreToolUse hook](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/guides/claude-code-pretooluse-hook-subagent-model/): How a Claude Code PreToolUse hook can change a tool call's input before it runs, so it can set a subagent's model. Payload, updatedInput, exit codes, testing.
- [When Claude Code's prompt cache goes cold, and what to do](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/guides/claude-code-prompt-cache/): How Claude Code prompt caching works: the 5-minute and 1-hour TTL, what invalidates the cache, what a cold send costs and when keeping it warm is worth a ping.
- [Claude Code Router or Downshift: a gateway and a hook solve different problems](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/guides/claude-code-router-vs-downshift/): Claude Code Router is a local gateway to many providers; Downshift is a hook that picks among the session's own models. How they differ and when to pick each.
- [Claude Code context packing for relevant code, opt-in](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/guides/claude-code-context-packing/): Give Claude Code less but better code context: symbol-level packing under a byte budget, opt-in. What is measured (latency, bytes) and what is not (quality).
- [Guias em português](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/pt-br/guias/): índice dos guias em português
- [Como economizar tokens no Claude Code, sem mito](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/pt-br/guias/economizar-tokens-claude-code/): Como gastar menos tokens no Claude Code: modelo, subagentes, cache de prompt e contexto. O que a documentação da Anthropic afirma e o que não está provado.
- [Qual modelo cada subagente usa no Claude Code](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/pt-br/guias/modelo-do-subagente-claude-code/): Como o Claude Code escolhe o modelo de um subagente: parâmetro da chamada, frontmatter, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL e modelo da sessão. Precedência e exemplo.
- [O limite de uso do Claude Code acaba rápido: de onde vem o consumo](https://downshift-ai.vercel.app/pt-br/guias/limite-de-uso-claude-code/): Por que o limite de 5 horas e o semanal do Claude Code acabam rápido: subagentes, cache frio, contexto longo. Como medir e o que ajustar, segundo a Anthropic.
